'''''Vicia acutifolia''''', commonly known as '''fourleaf vetch''' or '''sand vetch''', is a species of [[flowering plant]] in the family [[Fabaceae]]. It is native to the southeastern [[United States]] and the northern [[Bahamas]].<ref name="FSUS">{{cite web |title=Vicia acutifolia |url=https://fsus.ncbg.unc.edu/main.php?pg=show-taxon-detail.php&taxonid=2996 |publisher=Flora of the Southeastern United States |access-date=19 April 2026}}</ref>

== Description ==
''Vicia acutifolia'' is a [[perennial]] [[herb]] in the genus ''[[Vicia]]''. It produces [[pinnately compound]] leaves with multiple pairs of [[leaflet (botany)|leaflets]] and bears [[racemose]] [[inflorescences]] of [[papilionaceous]] flowers. The fruit is a [[legume]]. Within its range, it is distinguished from similar species such as ''[[Vicia floridana]]'' by its larger flowers and longer legumes.<ref name="FSUS" />

== Taxonomy ==
The species was described by [[Stephen Elliott (botanist)|Stephen Elliott]] in 1823 in ''A Sketch of the Botany of South-Carolina and Georgia'' (volume 2, page 225).<ref name="IPNI">{{cite web |title=Vicia acutifolia Elliott |url=https://www.ipni.org/n/524493-1 |publisher=International Plant Names Index |access-date=19 April 2026}}</ref> It is widely recognized as a distinct species in modern floristic treatments.<ref name="Atlas" /><ref name="FSUS" />

The species has also been placed in the genera ''Cracca'' and ''Ervum'' as ''Cracca acutifolia'' and ''Ervum acutifolium'', respectively, though these treatments are not widely adopted.<ref name="GBIF" /> Another synonym, ''Vicia lutescens'', has been used in some classifications.<ref name="GBIF" />

== Distribution and habitat ==
''Vicia acutifolia'' occurs from southeastern [[South Carolina]] south through [[Florida]] and west to the eastern [[Florida Panhandle]], with additional occurrences in the northern [[Bahamas]].<ref name="NS" /><ref name="FSUS" /> In Florida, it has been documented from numerous counties based on vouchered herbarium specimens.<ref name="Atlas" />

It inhabits moist environments, including pond margins, pine [[flatwoods]], hammocks, wet woodlands, and roadside [[ditches]].<ref name="NS" /><ref name="FSUS" />

Occurrence data compiled by the [[Global Biodiversity Information Facility]] (GBIF) indicate thousands of records across its range, including herbarium specimens and research-grade observations, reflecting its relative abundance.<ref name="GBIF" />

== Phenology ==
Flowering occurs from April to June.<ref name="FSUS" />

== Ecology ==
''Vicia acutifolia'' is associated with moist soils and is considered a facultative wetland species (FACW) in the Atlantic and Gulf Coastal Plain, indicating that it usually occurs in wetlands but may also be found in non-wetland habitats.<ref name="Atlas" /><ref name="FSUS" />

== Conservation ==
''Vicia acutifolia'' has a [[NatureServe]] global conservation rank of '''G4G5''', indicating that it is considered apparently secure to secure across its range, although the status has not been recently reviewed.<ref name="NS" /> The species is reported to be frequent and abundant in parts of its range, particularly in [[Florida]], [[Georgia (U.S. state)|Georgia]], and [[South Carolina]].<ref name="NS" />

Although it occurs in a variety of moist habitats and is not currently considered at high risk, continued monitoring is recommended due to uncertainty in long-term population trends.<ref name="NS" />
